newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM Cargo ups space to Spain due to truck strike.
newsitem.headline: KLM Cargo ups space to Spain due to truck strike.

text.p: A KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV Cargo spokesman said the Dutch airline is making more space available on its flights to Spain due to the worsening Spanish truckers strike.
"KLM does not seem to have too many problems at the moment, it is not severe. But the cargo streams are slowing down so we are flying more to Spain," he said.
Extra capacity is being made available in case the situation gets worse, he added.
Meanwhile a spokeswoman for the Dutch Airfreight Trucking Association (DATA) told Reuters that around 100 Dutch truckers are stranded in Spain due to the truckers strike.
"There is nothing we can do. It is getting worse every day and it is a very dangerous situation," she said
The DATA secretariat is also provided by the Interport trucking company, a specialist haulier operating to Spain and Portugal.
The spokeswoman said two of Interport's own drivers are stuck because of the strike - one in Northern Spain and one in Madrid.
The Dutch trucking company has now cancelled all of its services to Spain due to the dangerous situation, she added.
"The company's last truck to Spain left on Wednesday but we have now decided to cancel other services."
One of the Interport's trailers had already been damaged due to stones being thrown, she added.
Usually, the company has around nine trucks a week going to Spain.
"We are losing business to the airlines as many of our business is airfreight and perishables, so more cargo is being flown," she said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+ 542
